u3-l1.2.note.en: In Slovak homes the toilet (WC) is often a separate little room.
u3-l1.2.note.t: Slovakiyadagi uylarda hojatxona (WC) koʻpincha alohida kichik xonada boʻladi.

u3-l1.7.note.en: Also simply up and down. Kuchyňa je **hore**. = The kitchen is upstairs.
u3-l1.7.note.t: Oddiy «tepada – pastda» maʼnosida ham ishlatiladi. Kuchyňa je **hore**. = Oshxona yuqorida.

u3-l1.10.note.en: The desk at the entrance, where the porter (**vrátnik**) sits. In Emma's dorm, that's pán Kováč.
u3-l1.10.note.t: Kirishdagi stol, u yerda qorovul (**vrátnik**) oʻtiradi. Emmaning yotoqxonasida bu — janob Kovach.

u3-l1.12.note.en: **internát** = student dormitory. Emma and Lucia share a room there.
u3-l1.12.note.t: **internát** = talabalar yotoqxonasi. Emma va Lusiya u yerda bitta xonada yashashadi.

en: The room is upstairs and the kitchen is downstairs.
The room is upstairs and the kitchen downstairs.

u3-l1.16.question.en: Lucia wants to cook. Where does she go?
u3-l1.16.question.t: Lusiya ovqat pishirmoqchi. U qayerga boradi?

en: An adjective takes the gender of its noun: **-ý** for masculine, **-á** for feminine, **-é** for neuter.
The ending is the same before the noun (malá izba) and after je (Izba je malá).
t: Sifat oʻz otining jinsiga moslashadi: erkak jinsi uchun **-ý**, ayol jinsi uchun **-á**, oʻrta jins uchun **-é**. Oʻzbekchada sifat oʻzgarmaydi (katta xona, katta mashina), slovakchada esa oʻzgaradi.
Qoʻshimcha ot oldida ham (malá izba), je soʻzidan keyin ham (Izba je malá) bir xil boʻladi.

u3-l2.3.why.en: Izba ends in -a, so it's feminine and the adjective takes **-á**: veľk**á**. The ending is the same after je as before the noun.
u3-l2.3.why.t: Izba -a bilan tugaydi, demak ayol jinsida, sifat esa **-á** oladi: veľk**á**. je soʻzidan keyin ham qoʻshimcha ot oldidagidek boʻladi.

u3-l2.4.why.en: Balkón ends in a consonant, so it's masculine and takes **-ý**: mal**ý**. Malá goes with feminine nouns like izba, malé with neuter ones like auto.
u3-l2.4.why.t: Balkón undosh bilan tugaydi, demak erkak jinsida va **-ý** oladi: mal**ý**. Malá izba kabi ayol jinsidagi, malé esa auto kabi oʻrta jinsdagi otlar bilan keladi.

u3-l2.5.why.en: Kuchyňa ends in -a, so it's feminine and the adjective takes **-á**: nov**á**. Nový goes with masculine nouns, nové with neuter ones.
u3-l2.5.why.t: Kuchyňa -a bilan tugaydi, demak ayol jinsida, sifat esa **-á** oladi: nov**á**. Nový erkak jinsi, nové esa oʻrta jins uchun.

u3-l2.6.note.en: **pekný** = nice, pretty. **ale** = but. Pekný works the same way: pekn**á** izba.
u3-l2.6.note.t: **pekný** = chiroyli, yaxshi. **ale** = lekin. Pekný ham xuddi shunday oʻzgaradi: pekn**á** izba.

u3-l2.8.en.en: The room is small but nice.

en: To ask what something is like, use **aký?** It changes just like an adjective: **aký** (masculine), **aká** (feminine), **aké** (neuter).
t: Biror narsa qandayligini soʻrash uchun **aký?** ishlatiladi. U ham sifat kabi oʻzgaradi: **aký** (erkak jinsi), **aká** (ayol jinsi), **aké** (oʻrta jins).

u3-l2.10.why.en: **Aký?** changes like an adjective. Kúpeľňa ends in -a, so it's feminine: **aká**.
u3-l2.10.why.t: **Aký?** ham sifat kabi oʻzgaradi. Kúpeľňa -a bilan tugaydi, demak ayol jinsida: **aká**.

u3-l2.11.why.en: **Aký?** asks what something is like. Where? is **kde**: Kde je balkón?
u3-l2.11.why.t: **Aký?** narsa qandayligini soʻraydi. «Qayerda?» esa **kde**: Kde je balkón?

u3-l2.12.en.en: What's the car like? – It's old.

u3-l2.12.why.en: Auto ends in -o, so it's neuter and takes **-é**: star**é**. The question already shows it: **aké** je auto.
u3-l2.12.why.t: Auto -o bilan tugaydi, demak oʻrta jinsda va **-é** oladi: star**é**. Savol ham buni koʻrsatib turibdi: **aké** je auto.

en: The kitchen is old but nice.
The kitchen is old but pretty.

u3-l2.15.en.en: The dorm is big, but the kitchen is small.

u3-l2.15.why.en: Each adjective matches its own noun. Kuchyňa is feminine, so **malá**, even though veľký before it goes with internát, which is masculine.
u3-l2.15.why.t: Har bir sifat oʻz otiga moslashadi. Kuchyňa ayol jinsida, shuning uchun **malá**. Oldingi veľký esa erkak jinsidagi internát bilan keladi.

u3-l2.16.en.en: The room is big and nice.

u3-l3.0.note.en: Posteľ is feminine, even without -a: posteľ je mal**á**.
u3-l3.0.note.t: Posteľ ayol jinsida, garchi -a bilan tugamasa ham: posteľ je mal**á**.

u3-l3.5.note.en: Okno is neuter, like auto: okno je veľk**é**.
u3-l3.5.note.t: Okno oʻrta jinsda, xuddi auto kabi: okno je veľk**é**.

u3-l3.7.en.en: on the left – on the right

u3-l3.8.en.en: The desk is on the left.

u3-l3.9.en.en: The lamp is on the right.

u3-l3.10.en.en: at the front – at the back

u3-l3.11.question.en: How do you say “The wardrobe is at the back”?

u3-l3.12.prompt.en: The desk is on the left and the bed is on the right.

u3-l3.13.why.en: Okno ends in -o, so it's neuter, like auto, and takes **-é**: veľk**é**.
u3-l3.13.why.t: Okno -o bilan tugaydi, demak auto kabi oʻrta jinsda va **-é** oladi: veľk**é**.

u3-l3.14.why.en: Posteľ ends in a consonant but is feminine, so the adjective takes **-á**: nov**á**.
u3-l3.14.why.t: Posteľ undosh bilan tugasa ham, ayol jinsida, shuning uchun sifat **-á** oladi: nov**á**. Bu soʻzni jinsi bilan yodlab qoʻying.

en: The room is small but the window is big.
The room is small but the window is large.

u3-l3.16.en.en: The lamp is on the left.

en: Possessives match the gender of the thing owned, just like adjectives: môj stôl, moj**a** izba, moj**e** okno.
Watch the vowel: m**ô**j but m**o**ja, n**á**š but n**a**ša. Use **tvoj** with ty and **váš** with vy.
t: Egalik olmoshlari ham, sifatlar kabi, narsaning jinsiga moslashadi: môj stôl, moj**a** izba, moj**e** okno. Oʻzbekchada «mening» oʻzgarmaydi: mening stolim, mening xonam.
Unliga eʼtibor bering: m**ô**j, lekin m**o**ja; n**á**š, lekin n**a**ša. **tvoj** ty bilan, **váš** esa vy bilan ishlatiladi.

en: Your bed is on the left.
**jeho** (his), **jej** (her) and **ich** (their) never change. They go with any noun.
t: **jeho** (uning — erkakning), **jej** (uning — ayolning) va **ich** (ularning) hech qachon oʻzgarmaydi. Ular har qanday ot bilan ishlatiladi. Oʻzbekchada ikkalasi ham «uning», slovakchada esa farqlanadi.

u3-l4.2.why.en: Possessives match the gender of the thing owned. Izba is feminine, so **moja**. Watch the vowel: môj for masculine, but moja.
u3-l4.2.why.t: Egalik olmoshi narsaning jinsiga moslashadi (oʻzbekchada «mening» oʻzgarmaydi). Izba ayol jinsida, shuning uchun **moja**. Unliga eʼtibor bering: erkak jinsida môj, lekin moja.

u3-l4.3.why.en: Stôl is masculine, so it's **tvoj**. Tvoja goes with feminine nouns, tvoje with neuter ones.
u3-l4.3.why.t: Stôl erkak jinsida, shuning uchun **tvoj**. Tvoja ayol jinsidagi, tvoje esa oʻrta jinsdagi otlar bilan keladi.

u3-l4.6.en.en: His bed is on the left.

en: **Čí?** means whose. It matches the gender of the thing too: **čí** (masculine), **čia** (feminine), **čie** (neuter).
A short answer is just the possessive: Môj. Jej. Naše.
t: **Čí?** — «kimniki?». U ham narsaning jinsiga moslashadi: **čí** (erkak jinsi), **čia** (ayol jinsi), **čie** (oʻrta jins).
Qisqa javob — faqat egalik olmoshining oʻzi: Môj. Jej. Naše. (Meniki. Uniki. Bizniki.)

u3-l4.8.why.en: **Čí?** matches the thing it asks about. Posteľ is feminine, even without -a, so **čia**.
u3-l4.8.why.t: **Čí?** soʻralayotgan narsaga moslashadi. Posteľ -a bilan tugamasa ham ayol jinsida, shuning uchun **čia**.

u3-l4.9.question.en: “Čia je to skriňa?” Which answer fits?
u3-l4.9.question.t: «Čia je to skriňa?» Qaysi javob mos keladi?

u3-l4.9.why.en: The short answer keeps the gender of the thing: skriňa is feminine, so **moja**, just like čia. Môj is masculine, moje neuter.
u3-l4.9.why.t: Qisqa javob narsaning jinsini saqlaydi: skriňa ayol jinsida, shuning uchun **moja**, xuddi čia kabi. Môj erkak jinsi, moje esa oʻrta jins uchun.

u3-l4.11.why.en: Possessives match the thing owned. Skriňa is feminine, so **tvoja**. Tvoj goes with masculine nouns, tvoje with neuter ones.
u3-l4.11.why.t: Egalik olmoshi narsaga moslashadi. Skriňa ayol jinsida, shuning uchun **tvoja**. Tvoj erkak jinsidagi, tvoje oʻrta jinsdagi otlar bilan keladi.

u3-l4.12.en.en: Mrs Horváthová, is this your lamp?

u3-l4.12.why.en: You say vy to a teacher, so “your” is **vaša** (feminine, for lampa). Tvoja goes with ty, for friends.
u3-l4.12.why.t: Oʻqituvchiga vy (siz) deyiladi, shuning uchun «sizning» — **vaša** (lampa ayol jinsida). Tvoja esa «sening», ty bilan, doʻstlarga.

u3-l5.0.note.en: Marek, Lucia's brother, has a new flat. Byt is masculine: nov**ý** byt.
u3-l5.0.note.t: Lusiyaning akasi Marekning yangi kvartirasi bor. Byt erkak jinsida: nov**ý** byt.

u3-l5.1.note.en: To two or more people, or formally. To one friend: **Poď ďalej!**
u3-l5.1.note.t: Ikki yoki undan koʻp odamga yoki hurmat bilan aytiladi. Bitta doʻstga: **Poď ďalej!**

u3-l5.2.question.en: Marek opens the door for Emma and Lucia. What does he say?
u3-l5.2.question.t: Marek Emma va Lusiyaga eshikni ochdi. U nima deydi?

u3-l5.2.why.en: Marek is talking to two people, so he uses the vy form, with **-te**: Poď**te** ďalej! = Come in! To one friend it's Poď ďalej!
u3-l5.2.why.t: Marek ikki kishiga gapiryapti, shuning uchun **-te** bilan vy shaklini ishlatadi: Poď**te** ďalej! = Kiring! Bitta doʻstga Poď ďalej! deyiladi.

u3-l5.4.note.en: The full name is **obývacia izba**. Obývací is a soft adjective: it ends in **-í, -ia, -ie**, not -ý, -á, -é.
u3-l5.4.note.t: Toʻliq nomi — **obývacia izba**. Obývací — yumshoq sifat: u -ý, -á, -é emas, **-í, -ia, -ie** bilan tugaydi.

u3-l5.7.en.en: The hallway is in the middle.

u3-l5.8.en.en: The hallway is in the middle.

u3-l5.9.en.en: The bedroom is on the left and the living room on the right.
u3-l5.9.en.t: Yotoq xonasi chapda, mehmonxona esa oʻngda.

u3-l5.12.note.en: svetl**á** izba = a bright room, full of light
u3-l5.12.note.t: svetl**á** izba = yorugʻ xona, yorugʻlikka toʻla

u3-l5.13.en.en: The living room is big and bright.

u3-l5.13.why.en: Obývačka is feminine (it ends in -a), so both adjectives take **-á**: veľká a svetl**á**.
u3-l5.13.why.t: Obývačka ayol jinsida (-a bilan tugaydi), shuning uchun ikkala sifat ham **-á** oladi: veľká a svetl**á**.

en: The flat is nice but expensive.
The apartment is nice but expensive.
The flat is pretty but expensive.

u3-l5.16.en.en: The flat isn't expensive, it's cheap.

u3-l5.16.why.en: Byt is masculine (it ends in a consonant), so the adjective takes **-ý**: lacn**ý**, just like drahý.
u3-l5.16.why.t: Byt erkak jinsida (undosh bilan tugaydi), shuning uchun sifat **-ý** oladi: lacn**ý**, xuddi drahý kabi.

en: **Ktorý?** asks which one. It changes like an adjective: **ktorý** (masculine), **ktorá** (feminine), **ktoré** (neuter).
To answer, point with **ten**, **tá**, **to** (that one). Add **-to** for “this one here”: tento, táto, toto.
t: **Ktorý?** — «qaysi biri?». U sifat kabi oʻzgaradi: **ktorý** (erkak jinsi), **ktorá** (ayol jinsi), **ktoré** (oʻrta jins).
Javob berganda **ten**, **tá**, **to** (ana u) bilan koʻrsatiladi. «Mana bu» deyish uchun **-to** qoʻshiladi: tento, táto, toto.

en: Which desk is yours? – The one on the left.
Which bed is mine? – The one on the right.

u3-l6.1.why.en: **Ktorý?** changes like an adjective. Izba is feminine, so **ktorá**.
u3-l6.1.why.t: **Ktorý?** sifat kabi oʻzgaradi. Izba ayol jinsida, shuning uchun **ktorá**.

u3-l6.2.en.en: Which desk is mine? – The one at the front.

u3-l6.2.why.en: Point with the word that matches the noun: stôl is masculine, so **ten**. Tá is for feminine nouns, to for neuter ones.
u3-l6.2.why.t: Otga mos koʻrsatish soʻzini tanlang: stôl erkak jinsida, shuning uchun **ten**. Tá ayol jinsidagi, to oʻrta jinsdagi otlar uchun.

u3-l6.3.question.en: Lucia asks: “Ktorá lampa je tvoja?” Emma's lamp is on the left. What does Emma say?
u3-l6.3.question.t: Lusiya soʻraydi: «Ktorá lampa je tvoja?» Emmaning chirogʻi chapda. Emma nima deydi?

u3-l6.3.why.en: Lampa is feminine, so Emma points with **tá**, matching ktorá. Ten is masculine, to is neuter.
u3-l6.3.why.t: Lampa ayol jinsida, shuning uchun Emma ktorá kabi **tá** bilan koʻrsatadi. Ten erkak jinsi, to esa oʻrta jins uchun.

u3-l6.4.why.en: Okno is neuter, so the pointing word is to; for “this one here”, add -to: **toto**. Tento is masculine, táto feminine.
u3-l6.4.why.t: Okno oʻrta jinsda, shuning uchun koʻrsatish soʻzi to; «mana bu» uchun -to qoʻshiladi: **toto**. Tento erkak jinsi, táto ayol jinsi uchun.

en: To say whose, Slovak turns the name into an adjective. Men's names add **-ov**: Tomáš → Tomáš**ov**. Women's names drop the final -a and add **-in**: Emm**a** → Emm**in**, Luci**a** → Luci**in**.
Then add the ending for the thing owned: nothing for masculine, **-a** for feminine, **-o** for neuter.
t: «Kimniki» deyish uchun slovak tilida ism sifatga aylantiriladi (oʻzbekchadagi «-ning» oʻrniga). Erkaklar ismiga **-ov** qoʻshiladi: Tomáš → Tomáš**ov**. Ayollar ismida oxirgi -a tushib qoladi va **-in** qoʻshiladi: Emm**a** → Emm**in**, Luci**a** → Luci**in**.
Keyin narsaning jinsiga qarab qoʻshimcha qoʻshiladi: erkak jinsi uchun hech narsa, ayol jinsi uchun **-a**, oʻrta jins uchun **-o**.

en: Lucia's bed is on the left.

u3-l6.8.why.en: Byt is masculine, so Tomášov takes no ending: **Tomášov**. Tomášova goes with feminine nouns, Tomášovo with neuter ones.
u3-l6.8.why.t: Byt erkak jinsida, shuning uchun Tomášov qoʻshimcha olmaydi: **Tomášov**. Tomášova ayol jinsidagi, Tomášovo oʻrta jinsdagi otlar bilan keladi.

u3-l6.9.en.en: Lucia's bed is on the left.

u3-l6.9.why.en: Posteľ is feminine, even without -a, so Luciin adds **-a**: Luciin**a**.
u3-l6.9.why.t: Posteľ -a bilan tugamasa ham ayol jinsida, shuning uchun Luciin soʻziga **-a** qoʻshiladi: Luciin**a**.

u3-l6.10.why.en: Women's names drop -a and add **-in**: Emma → Emmin. Izba is feminine, so add -a: Emmin**a**. -ov is for men's names.
u3-l6.10.why.t: Ayollar ismida -a tushib qoladi va **-in** qoʻshiladi: Emma → Emmin. Izba ayol jinsida, shuning uchun yana -a qoʻshiladi: Emmin**a**. -ov esa erkaklar ismi uchun.

u3-l6.12.en.en: What's the flat like? – Big and bright.

u3-l6.12.why.en: The answer says what the flat is like, so the question is **Aký?** Ktorý asks which one, čí asks whose.
u3-l6.12.why.t: Javob kvartira qandayligini aytyapti, demak savol — **Aký?** Ktorý «qaysi biri?», čí esa «kimniki?» deb soʻraydi.

u3-l7.1.why.en: Kuchyňa is feminine, so the adjective takes **-á**: mal**á**, like naša before it.
u3-l7.1.why.t: Kuchyňa ayol jinsida, shuning uchun sifat **-á** oladi: mal**á**, oldidagi naša kabi.

u3-l7.2.en.en: The front desk is downstairs, on the left.

u3-l7.3.why.en: **Čia** is a form of čí?, whose. Which? would be ktorá, and what is it like? would be aká.
u3-l7.3.why.t: **Čia** — čí? (kimniki?) soʻzining shakli. «Qaysi?» ktorá, «qanday?» esa aká boʻlardi.

u3-l7.5.why.en: Stôl is masculine, so **tvoj**, just like ktorý. Tvoja goes with feminine nouns, tvoje with neuter ones.
u3-l7.5.why.t: Stôl erkak jinsida, shuning uchun **tvoj**, xuddi ktorý kabi. Tvoja ayol jinsidagi, tvoje oʻrta jinsdagi otlar bilan keladi.

en: Tomáš's flat is big and bright.
Tomáš's apartment is big and bright.

u3-l7.7.why.en: Lampa is feminine, so Emmin adds **-a**: Emmin**a**.
u3-l7.7.why.t: Lampa ayol jinsida, shuning uchun Emmin soʻziga **-a** qoʻshiladi: Emmin**a**.

u3-l7.8.question.t: «Aká je izba?» savoliga qaysi javob mos keladi?

u3-l7.8.why.en: **Aká?** asks what the room is like, so the answer describes it. Tá vľavo answers ktorá (which one), and Moja answers čia (whose).
u3-l7.8.why.t: **Aká?** xona qandayligini soʻraydi, shuning uchun javob uni tasvirlaydi. Tá vľavo — ktorá (qaysi biri?) savoliga, Moja esa čia (kimniki?) savoliga javob.

u3-l7.11.en.en: Which bed is Lucia's? – The one on the right.

u3-l7.11.why.en: The answer points to one bed, tá vpravo, so the question is which one. Posteľ is feminine: **ktorá**.
u3-l7.11.why.t: Javob bitta karavotni koʻrsatyapti (tá vpravo), demak savol «qaysi biri?». Posteľ ayol jinsida: **ktorá**.

u3-l7.12.en.en: Mrs Horváthová, is this your desk?

u3-l7.12.why.en: Stôl is masculine, so **váš**. Vaša and vaše go with feminine and neuter nouns. It's váš, not tvoj, because you say vy to a teacher.
u3-l7.12.why.t: Stôl erkak jinsida, shuning uchun **váš**. Vaša va vaše ayol va oʻrta jinsdagi otlar bilan keladi. Oʻqituvchiga vy deyilgani uchun tvoj emas, váš.

u3-l7.13.prompt.en: The bathroom is on the right and the kitchen is at the back.
